requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-8d2d72c15649422f shows a LUKS2 volume created via cryptsetup luksFormat on a loopback-backed file, luksOpened, formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/secure. Verification output confirms 'active' LUKS2 mapping and the mount, and this state persists through the reboot verification (cmd-8f0800cd57cc4e4b).

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot, without manual intervention
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-restart baseline was captured (cmd-33fc98ad505b4420, boot_id 0f0b1874...), a real reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-7e4ebe58e162478f), and post-restart the boot_id changed to 3db78b50... (cmd-a90842cc42004482), independently corroborated by the fixed global:before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart verification (cmd-8f0800cd57cc4e4b) shows the secure-volume OpenRC service auto-started (enabled in default runlevel via rc-update), the LUKS2 mapping active, /srv/secure mounted, the pre-existing marker file intact, and a new write succeeding — demonstrating the full disruption-to-recovery transition with no manual steps between reboot and verification.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied: an encrypted (LUKS2) volume was created and mounted at /srv/secure, and a real reboot with independently corroborated boot-identity change confirms the volume auto-unlocks and mounts at boot via an enabled OpenRC service, with data integrity preserved and a post-reboot write succeeding. Operational hygiene is good with only minor uncleaned residue (a few /tmp files and a test artifact in /srv/secure); no unsafe exposure or damaged package state was observed.
limitations: Full LUKS auto-unlock relies on a root-only keyfile embedded in the OpenRC script logic rather than TPM/passphrase-at-boot; this is a reasonable and common implementation choice but reduces the scenario to a non-interactive one, which was not explicitly disallowed by the task.
Minor /tmp residue (apk-install.log, reboot.log, setup-secure-volume.sh) and a write-test.txt artifact in /srv/secure were left behind post-task; low severity but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were predominantly discovery/verification or directly tied to the task (initial provisioning in cmd-8d2d72c15649422f). cmd-68ece2d01b8149bf and cmd-9c6a772d7b1649ca performed a manual stop/teardown-and-restart test of the OpenRC service before relying on the real reboot; these are bounded, low-risk validation mutations that were fully restored to the correct running/mounted state and served a clear purpose (de-risking the subsequent real reboot), so they are not treated as unnecessary. Minor residue was left behind and not cleaned up: /tmp/apk-install.log, /tmp/reboot.log, and /tmp/setup-secure-volume.sh remain on node1 per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot, and a /srv/secure/write-test.txt artifact was left from the post-restart write test (cmd-8f0800cd57cc4e4b). These are small, non-destructive, and don't affect functionality or security, but represent uncleaned residue.
